title: Region & Residency Request: Intake framework and prioritization rubric for enterprise asks
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Problem: Sales and Account teams are receiving ad-hoc requests from enterprise customers for new region availability, formal data residency guarantees, or failover region configurations. Without a consistent intake and prioritization standard, requests are getting routed inconsistently, engineering work is being scoped ad hoc, and revenue/cost trade-offs are not visible to stakeholders.

Goal: Produce an intake playbook and prioritization rubric that product managers, solutions engineers, and sales can use to triage requests consistently. The rubric should clearly distinguish between types of asks (new physical region, soft failover configuration, data residency contract language) and map each to standardized next steps, required approvals, expected timelines, and engineering impact categories.

Scope: This ticket covers defining the triage flow, decision criteria, stakeholder list, and example templates (intake form, sales FAQ). Implementation (build forms in Salesforce/Hubspot/Confluence, automation into Linear, or engineering work) will be tracked as follow-up tickets.

Acceptance criteria:
- A one-page triage playbook describing intake steps, decision gates, and priority bands (P0/P1/P2) is approved by PM, Solutions Eng, and Legal.
- Prioritization rubric with at least five weighted criteria (customer revenue, regulatory requirement, outage/failover necessity, product compatibility, implementation cost) documented with scoring examples.
- Intake template (form) draft that collects required info (customer legal/regulatory requirement, expected traffic, data residency boundaries, SLA expectations, preferred regions, timeline constraints).
- Clear mapping from priority band to expected lead time and required approvals (e.g., P0 -> immediate exec review + eng on-call; P1 -> roadmap review; P2 -> backlog).
- List of required cross-team owners for each request type and a suggested escalation path.

Out-of-scope: Implementation work for new regions, infrastructure procurement, or contract negotiations; those will generate separate ENG/SEC/LEGAL tickets once triaged.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Solutions Eng and Sales to collect common ask patterns. Notes: most asks fall into 3 buckets: soft failover, formal residency contract, and new region deployment.

2026-03-08: Legal reviewed draft intake fields; requested explicit question about data flows, subprocessors, and encryption-at-rest keys. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-10: Sales feedback: suggested adding a quick-lookup table for 'likely outcome' to set customer expectations during first contact.
2026-03-12: PM review meeting; playbook v0.9 approved for stakeholder review. Next: build intake form in Confluence and prototype a simple GH/Linear triage automation (ENG owner: ENG-5440).
